chunks: Hadith 136 — And in the narration of Zayd al-Shahham and al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who performed wudu (ablution) and then forgot to wipe over his head until he had stood in salat (prayer), he said: “Then let him leave, wipe his head, and repeat the prayer.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer to be repeated
key_terms.رَأْسِهِ: his head, the place to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.فَلْيَنْصَرِفْ: let him leave or withdraw from the prayer
key_terms.وَلْيُعِدِ: let him repeat or perform again
key_terms.يَمْسَحَ: to wipe as part of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgot to wipe his head in wudu (ablution) until after starting salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who omitted wiping the head during wudu (ablution) and only remembered after beginning salat (prayer). It indicates that the omitted act must be completed and the salat (prayer) repeated, showing the necessity of proper ritual purity for valid worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.136 - In the narration of Zayd al-Shahham and al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), concerning a man who performs wudu but forgets to wipe his head until he has started the prayer,
Imam (as) said: "Let him leave, wipe his head, and repeat the prayer."
